blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Strategic due diligence goes far beyond the sanctions screen and the credit check. It seeks to understand the counterparty the way a serious investor would: who really owns the business, how the cash flows actually work, where the vulnerabilities sit, how the company has behaved under stress in the past, and what picture emerges when everything is placed side by side.

A good strategic review uses many sources: public filings, local press, court records, industry relationships, former employees, and first-hand site visits. None of these is decisive alone; together, they form a portrait that is almost always more honest than anything the counterparty would voluntarily share. Disagreements between sources are the most interesting part, not an inconvenience.

The object is not to decide yes or no. The object is to decide on what terms. A well-understood counterparty can still be a good partner, provided the structure of the deal reflects the risks that the diligence has revealed. The worst outcome is to enter a deal having done everything quickly, and understood nothing slowly.

items.q: According to the text, what is the object of strategic due diligence?
options: To decide on what terms to proceed
To decide a simple yes or no
items.why: "The object is not to decide yes or no. The object is to decide on what terms."

items.q: How does the author regard disagreements between sources?
options: As an inconvenience to be resolved
As the most interesting part of the review
As a sign the diligence has failed
As proof the counterparty is dishonest
items.why: "Disagreements between sources are the most interesting part, not an inconvenience."

items.q: What does the text say about the individual sources used in a review?
options: A single site visit is decisive
None is decisive alone, but together they form a portrait
Public filings outweigh all other sources
Only former employees can be trusted
items.why: "None of these is decisive alone; together, they form a portrait…"

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A partner should be judged on the terms of the deal, not in the abstract
A clean sanctions screen is enough to clear a counterparty
Site visits can reveal what filings do not
Conflicting evidence is worth examining closely
items.why: Inferência: o texto abre dizendo que a diligência vai muito além do sanctions screen — logo o autor discorda que ele baste.

items.q: The line "understood nothing slowly" suggests that the author values…
options: understanding over the mere appearance of thoroughness
avoiding site visits to save time
items.why: Inferência: o pior desfecho é ter feito tudo rápido e entendido nada — o autor prioriza a compreensão real, não a aparência de rigor.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte conduzindo a equipe de diligência. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, before anyone drafts a recommendation, let me be clear about what I expect from this file. We are not here to tick boxes. In this market, half the public information is either stale or quietly managed, so I want us to treat every clean document with a degree of healthy suspicion.

Here is what struck me on the site visit. The accounts we were sent show a business running comfortably, yet the plant I walked through last week was operating at maybe sixty per cent, and two of the shifts had been let go. That gap is precisely the sort of disagreement I want us chasing, not smoothing over.

So, three things. First, pull the court records directly rather than relying on the summary the counterparty provided. Second, find me two former employees who left in the last eighteen months — people talk once they are out. Third, cross-check the cash story against what we actually saw on the ground.

And remember why we are doing this. I am not trying to kill the deal. I am trying to work out the terms on which it becomes sensible. A partner we genuinely understand, structured properly, is worth far more than a flawless one we have simply taken on trust.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Charlotte want the team to treat clean documents with suspicion?
options: Because the counterparty refused to share them
Because in this market public information is often stale or quietly managed
Because the documents were filed too recently
Because the credit check had already failed
items.why: "half the public information is either stale or quietly managed, so I want us to treat every clean document with a degree of healthy suspicion."

items.q: What discrepancy did Charlotte notice on the site visit?
options: The accounts showed a comfortable business, but the plant ran at about sixty per cent
The plant was fully staffed but the accounts showed losses
The court records contradicted the credit check
Two shifts had been added despite falling demand
items.why: "The accounts… show a business running comfortably, yet the plant… was operating at maybe sixty per cent…"

items.q: Why does she want the team to find former employees?
options: To hire them for the new venture
Because people speak more openly once they have left
Because they still hold company shares
items.why: "find me two former employees… people talk once they are out."

items.q: What does Charlotte imply about the deal itself?
options: She has already decided to reject it
She is trying to establish the terms on which it makes sense, not to kill it
She believes it is flawless as presented
She wants to accept it on trust to save time
items.why: Inferência: "I am not trying to kill the deal. I am trying to work out the terms on which it becomes sensible."

items.q: What can be inferred about Charlotte's view of a 'flawless' counterparty taken on trust?
options: She prefers it to a partner the team actually understands
She values it less than a well-understood partner structured properly
She thinks it removes the need for site visits
She regards it as the safest possible outcome
items.why: Inferência: ela diz que um parceiro genuinamente entendido e bem estruturado vale muito mais do que um impecável aceito por confiança.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We pulled the court records before signing anything." Court records are…
options: press releases issued by the company
items.why: Court records = registros judiciais: documentos oficiais de processos e disputas.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The numbers looked fine on paper, but a ___ told us the plant was half idle."
items.why: Site visit = visita in loco: ver a operação de perto revela o que os papéis escondem.

items.q: "We wanted a first-hand account, not a summary passed through three people." First-hand means…
options: obtained directly from the original source
items.why: First-hand = em primeira mão: obtido diretamente da fonte original.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The diligence exposed a clear ___ in the counterparty's funding, which we then addressed in the deal structure."
items.why: Vulnerability = vulnerabilidade: o ponto fraco que a diligência expõe.

items.q: "How has the business behaved under stress in previous downturns?" Under stress means…
items.why: Under stress = sob estresse: em condições adversas, quando o negócio é testado.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em processos de diligência e negociação. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The committee still has to sign off on the diligence report." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Don't take the summary at face value — dig into the primary records." To dig into means to…
items.why: Dig into = investigar a fundo, escarafunchar.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the proposed terms." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed the plan, but the local team never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A clean sanctions screen alone won't move the needle on our confidence in this counterparty." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
